name: website-hero-loop
title: Website hero loop
summary: A silent, seamless loop of 4 to 20 seconds that plays behind a website's hero section: picture only, no words, no audio track.
use_when: A homepage or landing page wants motion behind its headline. The headline itself stays in the page's HTML.

pace.note: A hero loop has no voice; the ceiling is here for completeness.

beats.name: loop
beats.job: One continuous motion that ends exactly where it began, so the seam never shows.

rules: Calm enough to sit behind a headline: no flashes, nothing that competes with the words beside it.
The subject stays in the centre that survives every window shape (see the website safe zone).

loop.poster: The loop's calmest frame, also shown instead of the loop when the viewer prefers reduced motion.
rules: Author the motion as a cycle whose period is the film's length: the last frame flows into the first.
Ship no audio track at all: browsers autoplay silent video, and a silent track only adds bytes.
The page gives the loop a pause control (WCAG 2.2.2: moving content longer than five seconds that starts on its own).
Under prefers-reduced-motion, the page shows the poster instead of playing the loop.
Words go in the page's HTML, where they stay accessible, translatable and sharp at every size.

deliver: MP4: H.264, yuv420p, moov atom first (faststart)

files.label: hero loop, MP4 (H.264)
files.note: Every browser plays it; no audio track, so it may autoplay.

files.label: hero loop, WebM (VP9)
files.note: Listed first in the page's <video> sources where the browser takes it: smaller at the same quality.

encode.note: Keep the files small: a hero loop loads before anything else on the page.

loudness.note: No audio track: browsers only autoplay muted or silent video.

captions.note: Nothing is spoken, so there is nothing to caption.

budget.note: A silent loop spends no voice or score credits. If a generated plate would genuinely help, the requester turns generation on and raises the budget.

sources.title: web.dev: Replace animated GIFs with video for faster page loads
sources.says: <video autoplay loop muted playsinline>, an H.264 MP4 and a VP9 WebM source.

sources.title: MDN: Autoplay guide for media and Web Audio APIs
sources.says: Autoplay is allowed for video with no audio track or muted audio; Safari needs playsinline.

sources.title: W3C: Understanding SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide
sources.says: Moving content that starts automatically, lasts more than five seconds and sits beside other content needs a way to pause, stop or hide it.

sources.title: MDN: prefers-reduced-motion
sources.says: Detects that the viewer asked to minimize non-essential motion.
